key_insight: V-PaSS improves prediction for unfamiliar perovskite solar cells by representing absorber alloys and device stacks with physically informed features rather than arbitrary labels.
engineering_relevance: The approach could help screen new absorber compositions and transport-layer combinations before fabrication.
method: Interpolate relaxed crystal graphs of 23 pure ABX₃ endpoints using Vegard’s law and learned bandgap bowing.
Encode layer sequence, cell polarity, and interfacial band offsets.
Represent chemical descriptions with a scientific language model.
evidence_signal: On institution-grouped tests using devices from unseen laboratories, untuned V-PaSS achieved 2.861% MAE versus 3.017% for a gradient-boosted baseline, with reported error reductions of 15.7–19.0% on unseen absorber alloys.
watch_item: Benchmark extrapolation does not establish prospective experimental accuracy; implementation also requires endpoint crystal graphs and reliable interface descriptors.
paper_title: Virtual-Alloy Physics-Aware Semantic System for extrapolative prediction of perovskite solar cells
